newsitem.title: BRAZIL: At least 14 people die in Brazil train crash.
newsitem.headline: At least 14 people die in Brazil train crash.

text.p: At least 14 people were killed and 40 injured when two trains collided in Brazil's Rio de Janeiro state on Wednesday morning, a spokeswoman for the federal railway network (RFFSA) said.

RFFSA spokeswoman Regina Digna said a train carrying copper crashed with a commuter train between Barra de Pirai and Japeri at 8:20 (1120 GMT) local time. The crash appeared to have been caused by faulty brakes on the copper train, which derailed and slammed into the passenger train, according to Joao Carlos, a disaster relief official.
He said several injured passengers were in life threatening condition in a local hospital. Rescue workers were at the scene but no more people were thought trapped in the train wreckage, he added.
The copper train consisted of 18 freight cars and a locomotive, while the commuter train had three cars and a locomotive, Digna said.
